subtitle: From Idea to Submission in 7 Days
author: Arthur AI Agent System
executive_summary: This workflow replaces the ad-hoc process that produced 23 versions over 3 weeks. Based on lessons from the MKG-RAG Second Brain paper journey, it targets 3 drafts in 7 days with higher novelty and fewer iterations. Key improvements: experiments-first approach, upfront novelty validation, venue-first planning, batched reviews, and quality gates from day 1.
key_findings: v1-v9 built on proxy/synthetic claims. Real experiments (DDXPlus) didn't arrive until v15-v17. Papers without real results get destroyed in review.
"Second Brain" was marketing until v23 when grounded in Extended Mind theory. Reviewers see through ungrounded framing immediately.
QUALITY_LOCKS and 3-agent review gate created AFTER the v9 crisis (score dropped from 8.5 to 4.4). Should have been there from the start.
23 versions, most were incremental patches. Each review-fix cycle costs time and introduces regression risk.
Started targeting Information Fusion, pivoted to AIiH. Format conversion (IEEE to LNCS) wasted multiple versions.
Clark & Chalmers Extended Mind, Hutchins Distributed Cognition added in final versions. Should anchor novelty claims from the beginning.

analysis.Phase 1: Foundation (Day 1-2): Tasks: Pick target venue (format, page limit, scope, deadline). Literature gap analysis: define novel contribution in ONE sentence. Run "Does this exist?" check (Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, arXiv). Build baseline experiments with real data. Design ablation-ready architecture (each component removable). Create comparison table: what existing methods do vs what yours adds. Anchor method in existing theory (not just a name — cite cognitive science, information theory, etc.).
analysis.Phase 2: Full Draft (Day 3-5): Tasks: Write complete paper with real results (not placeholders). All sections: intro, related work, method, experiments, discussion, conclusion. Include all tables, figures, equations. Apply venue format from the start (e.g., llncs.cls, IEEE template). 3-agent parallel review (peer-reviewer, methodology-expert, technical-writer). Batch ALL fixes into single revision (Draft 2). Rule: ALL THREE must pass. No exceptions. No "ship it with one approval."
analysis.Phase 3: Polish & Submit (Day 6-7): Tasks: Apply all Draft 2 review fixes. Final 3-agent review (should be minor issues only). Format compliance check (page count, references, anonymization). Generate supplementary materials if needed. Submit.
analysis.Quality Gates (Active from Day 1): QUALITY_LOCKS: Lock any element praised by reviewers. Never regress. POSITIVE_FEEDBACK tracker: Cumulative praise log across review rounds. Three-Agent Review Gate: Every draft reviewed by 3 agents in parallel. Unanimous approval required. Novelty Checkpoint: Before Phase 2, verify the one-sentence novelty claim still holds after literature review. Claims-Evidence Alignment: Every claim in the paper must map to a specific experiment, table, or citation. No orphan claims.
analysis.Novelty Boosters: Ablation-First Design: Build experiments so each component can be independently removed. Creates "unique contribution per component" — reviewers always ask for this. Theoretical Grounding Early: Don't just name your method — anchor it in established theory from draft 1. Examples: Extended Mind (Clark & Chalmers), Distributed Cognition (Hutchins), Information Foraging Theory. Comparison Table in Outline: Before writing, create a table of existing methods and what yours uniquely adds. If no clear gap, rethink the contribution. Real-World Framing: Position contribution as solving a real problem, not just improving metrics. "Why does this matter to a doctor/engineer/user?" Honest Limitations: Proactively state what your method does NOT do. Builds credibility and prevents reviewer attacks.

recommendations: Novelty claim is one sentence, grounded in theory
All experiments use real data (no proxies)
Ablation study shows each component's unique contribution
Statistical tests applied (Wilson CIs, McNemar's, etc.)
External baselines included (not just your own variants)
Double-blind compliance (no author names, no self-citations revealing identity)
conclusion: This v2 workflow addresses all major issues identified in the MKG-RAG journey: Honesty > Impressive Claims - Conceptual papers can be publishable without fake results. Quality Locks Prevent Regression - 23 locks ensured improvements were cumulative. Three Parallel Reviewers catch different issues: baselines, statistics, readability. ML Baselines Beating RAG Is Okay - Frame as accuracy vs generalization trade-off. Medical Datasets > General Benchmarks - Domain-specific data makes contribution tangible. Verify Numbers Before Locking - Wrong numbers hurt more than vague ones. Venue Selection Matters - Focused venue (AIiH) better than broad (Information Fusion). "Second Brain" Grounding - Marketing language became theoretical contribution when grounded in Extended Mind thesis. Never deliver without full team review - One-agent papers get rejected.
